messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] SEM and Multilevel Models in R and Mplus with AI - livestream seminar
messages.subject_clean: SEM and Multilevel Models in R and Mplus with AI - livestream seminar
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone

Instats is excited to offer a 2-day seminar, SEM in R and Mplus with AI <https://instats.org/seminar/sem-in-r-and-mplus-with-ai>, running August 13?14. This practice-oriented workshop introduces structural equation modeling for researchers who want to move confidently from regression-based approaches to latent variable modeling in Mplus and R using lavaan. A distinctive feature of the seminar is its integration of generative AI tools, including Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot, to support SEM coding, troubleshooting, interpretation, and reproducible research workflows in a transparent and methodologically responsible way. 

The seminar is part of a 2-part sereies on SEM and Multilevel Models in R and Mplus with AI <https://instats.org/course/sem-and-multilevel-models-in-r-and-mplus1>, with the multilevel modeling seminar running August 20?21. By purchasing both seminars, participants save 10% on their regular price. After completing the full course, you will have a full understanding of how to model complex datasets that involve multiple variables at multilevel levels of analysis ? including Multilevel SEM applications in R and Mplus.

Sign up today <https://instats.org/course/sem-and-multilevel-models-in-r-and-mplus1> to secure your spot, and feel free to share this opportunity with colleagues and students who might benefit!


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director
Institute for Statistical and Data Science

messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] Causal Roadmaps for Epidemiologic Analysis
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

A reminder - Sound epidemiologic evidence begins by specifying the comparison a study can support. Data Can Deceive: Causal Roadmaps is a seminar livestreaming August 5 with Robert Platt (School of Population and Global Health, McGill University), Kathryn Morrison (Precision Analytics), and Andy Wilson (Spencer Fox Eccles School of Medicine, University of Utah). Define epidemiologic estimands, assess identification conditions, and connect a research question to an implementable statistical analysis. Use target-trial thinking to specify eligibility, treatment strategies, time zero, outcomes, and follow-up when working with cohort, registry, or administrative data in R. Interpret adjustment and targeted-learning choices against explicit causal assumptions and communicate their limitations clearly.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/data-can-deceive-causal-roadmaps
Please circulate this reminder if it is relevant to colleagues or students.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director

messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] Spatial Statistics in R for Epidemiology
messages.subject_clean: Spatial Statistics in R for Epidemiology
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

Place and time can shape the patterns visible in epidemiological data. Spatial Statistics in R led by Nick Bearman (University College London and Geospatial Training Solutions) is now available as an on-demand streaming seminar. Analyse geographically referenced epidemiological data using GeoDa and R, from exploratory displays to spatial regression. Interpret spatial autocorrelation with Moran?s I and Local Indicators of Spatial Association to investigate geographic patterning. Apply clustering measures and space-time regression techniques when studying relationships across places and periods.

Course details: https://instats.org/seminar/spatial-statistics-in-r-1
Further information is available on the Instats course page.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director

messages.subject_clean: Spatial Data and R for Epidemiology
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

A reminder - Place-based patterns are often central to interpreting epidemiological evidence. Introduction to Spatial Data and R as a GIS 2.0 is a 2-day seminar livestreaming August 18?19 with Nick Bearman (University College London and Geospatial Training Solutions). Import, manage, process, and visualise spatial data in R and RStudio. Create choropleth and interactive maps, work with spatial objects, and automate repeated mapping tasks. Apply these workflows to map and communicate geographic patterns in epidemiological data.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/introduction-to-spatial-data-and-r-as-a-4
Full details are available on the Instats seminar page.


Best wishes

Professor and Director

messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] Advanced R spatial epidemiology analysis
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

Geographic context can alter how epidemiological patterns are assembled, compared, and interpreted. Advanced R for Spatial Analysis led by Nick Bearman (University College London and Geospatial Training Solutions) is now available as an on-demand streaming seminar. Use spatial joins, buffers, point-in-polygon operations, intersections, overlays, and area-weighted joins to integrate complex geographic data in R. Compare point and polygon representations and manipulate spatial datasets to investigate exposure, service access, and other epidemiological patterns. Apply these operations to connect mapped context with analytical questions in public-health research.

Course details: https://instats.org/seminar/advanced-r-for-spatial-analysis-1
Please circulate this information if it is relevant to colleagues or students.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director

messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] R package development for epidemiology
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

A reminder - Reusable analytical tools can make epidemiological work easier to check and collaborate on. R Package Development (Free Seminar) is a seminar livestreaming August 18 with Statistical Society of Canada (Statistical Society of Canada). Transform epidemiological R scripts into maintainable packages with organised code, unit tests, and documentation. Configure GitHub-based version control and automated testing workflows to support collaborative analytical development. Apply these practices to statistical analysis and display tools that epidemiology teams can review, reuse, and maintain.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/r-package-development-free-seminar
Please circulate this reminder if it is relevant to colleagues or students.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director

messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] UMAP and Dimensionality Reduction
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

High-dimensional epidemiological data can be difficult to explore without losing meaningful structure. Dimensionality Reduction with UMAP and Beyond 2.0 led by Nikolay Oskolkov (Lund University) is now available as an on-demand streaming seminar. Preprocess high-dimensional data and compare PCA, tSNE, UMAP, autoencoders, and related linear and nonlinear approaches. Implement and interpret dimension-reduction workflows in R and Python, including attention to tuning choices, structure preservation, and common pitfalls. Apply these methods to epidemiological datasets to explore multivariate patterns before subsequent modelling or visualisation.

Course details: https://instats.org/seminar/dimensionality-reduction-with-umap-and-b-1
Please circulate this information if it is relevant to colleagues or students.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director
